sections.h2: Where is the Buncombe County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
The Buncombe County Register of Deeds is at 205 College Street in Asheville, NC 28801, open Monday through Friday from 8 am to 5 pm. The recording and real estate desk answers at 828-250-4302, the vital records desk at 828-250-4300, and the help desk at 828-250-4303. A Spanish-language line is listed at 828-250-4307.

The county posts a holiday closing calendar on the office's web page, so check it before planning a same-day recording around Thanksgiving or the December holidays. The county's website now sits at buncombenc.gov, and older buncombecounty.org links forward there.

Records themselves go back to the 1700s. The public record search room at the College Street office is open the same 8 am to 5 pm weekday hours for anyone who prefers to look at records in person.

sections.h2: What does the Buncombe County Register of Deeds record?
sections.html:
It records the paper trail for land in the county: deeds, deeds of trust, cancellations of deeds of trust, powers of attorney, assumed business names, plats, UCC filings, separation agreements and road maintenance agreements. All of it is open for public inspection.

The office states that it is a record keeper only. By law its staff do not draft or change documents, though it supplies forms for satisfactions and assumed names. Anyone who needs a deed written, or has a question about what a document does, is told to hire an attorney. The office can record only originals that carry original signatures and proof of acknowledgment from a notary.

  • Real estate conveyances and deeds of trust
  • Satisfactions and cancellations after payoff
  • Plats and miscellaneous maps
  • Assumed names and UCC filings
  • Powers of attorney and related papers

sections.h2: What format rules apply to a deed in Buncombe County?
sections.html:
A deed must be on 8.5 by 11 or 8.5 by 14 inch paper with a three inch blank space at the top of the first page and at least half an inch of margin on the other sides. The rest of the pages need half inch margins on every side.

  • Black ink on white paper in a legible font of 9 points or larger.
  • Text on one side of the sheet only.
  • The type of instrument written at the top of page one.
  • No highlighter over important information.
  • Color or grayscale images count as non-standard.

Anything that misses these standards can still be recorded for $25 on top of the regular fee. Because that surcharge applies even to a clean legal document with a stray color scan, ask your closing attorney to print the final deed on plain white paper.

sections.h2: How much are recording fees and copies in Buncombe County?
sections.html:
Recording fees in Buncombe County are the uniform amounts fixed by state law, while copy charges are set locally. The table below lists each charge as the official pages print it.

Charges you may meet when recording or copying records in Buncombe County

Recording a general instrument$26.00 for 15 pages, $4.00 per added pageG.S. 161-10
Deed of trust or mortgage$64.00 for 35 pages, $4.00 per added pageG.S. 161-10
Satisfaction of a deed of trustNo feeG.S. 161-10
Non-standard document$25 plus the regular feeBuncombe County recording page

Non-certified copy$0.25 per pageBuncombe County recording page

For a copy by mail, send a check or money order payable to Register of Deeds with the Real Estate Records Request Form to 205 College Street, Asheville, NC 28801. A stamped, self-addressed envelope speeds the return.

sections.h2: Who pays transfer tax on a Buncombe County sale?
sections.html:
The seller. North Carolina charges the excise tax to the transferor, who pays it to the register of deeds before the deed is recorded, at one dollar per $500 of the price or fractional part.

Of each dollar collected, half goes to the county general fund and the rest is sent monthly to the state, less refunds and the county's allowance. Ask the closing attorney to show the excise tax line on your settlement statement before you sign, because the figure depends on the price stated on the deed.

The same state chapter also covers a parcel that sits in more than one county. The tax goes to the county that holds the greater value of that land.

sections.h2: Can I record electronically in Buncombe County?
sections.html:
Yes, for companies. Buncombe County accepts eRecording from financial and legal companies, attorneys and surveyors who sign up with one of its authorized providers.

The submitting company must complete a Submitter Memorandum of Understanding after choosing a provider. For a home seller, this usually matters only because it explains how a title firm can get your deed on record the same day it is signed. Individual owners can still bring originals to College Street or mail them in.

Recorded documents are searchable through the county's online records search, and the office posts a video tutorial for using it. The search covers deeds, deeds of trust, powers of attorney and assumed names, and the results can be viewed and printed.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures say about Buncombe County?
sections.html:
Buncombe County had an estimated 277,417 residents on July 1, 2025, about 3.0% above the 2020 base, with 142,799 housing units. The county covers 656.50 square miles of land and has 410.4 people per square mile.

The 2020 to 2024 survey shows an owner-occupied rate of 66.2% and a median owner-occupied home value of $391,800. Median gross rent is $1,362 a month, median household income is $74,436 and the mean travel time to work is 21.1 minutes. About 45.9% of adults 25 and older hold a bachelor's degree or higher. The county permitted 2,028 buildings in 2025.

Renters hold about a third of homes, so some sellers are investors with tenants in place. A lease does not change what the register records, but tell your closing attorney about it early.

Source: Census QuickFacts for Buncombe County.

sections.h2: What should an Asheville-area seller check before the deed is recorded?
sections.html:
Confirm three things: the deed format, the excise tax figure and the status of unpaid property tax. G.S. 47-18 says an unrecorded conveyance has no force against lien creditors or purchasers for value until it is registered in the county where the land lies, so the recording time sets priority.

Buncombe County's tax bills are normally due September 1 with a grace period that runs to the following January 5, so a closing in autumn may involve a tax bill that has been issued but not yet paid. The county tax office takes questions about property tax collections at 828-250-4910, and the county's separate property tax page covers the 2026 reappraisal delay in detail.

Before you list or accept an offer, pull your own deed from the online search so you can check the legal description and any easements. If an old mortgage was paid off years ago, look for the recorded satisfaction and ask the lender to file one if it is missing.

faqs.q: What are the Buncombe County Register of Deeds hours?
faqs.a: The office at 205 College Street in Asheville is open Monday through Friday, 8 am to 5 pm. The office follows the county holiday closing calendar, which is posted on its web page.

faqs.q: Does the Buncombe County Register of Deeds prepare deeds?
faqs.a: No. By state law the office only records documents and keeps the records, and it cannot draft or change them. It supplies forms for satisfactions and assumed names, and it tells people who need a deed written to hire an attorney.

faqs.q: How much does a certified copy of a deed cost in Buncombe County?
faqs.a: A certified copy costs $5 for the first page and $2 for each added page. A non-certified copy is $0.25 per page. Mail requests go to 205 College Street with a check or money order payable to Register of Deeds.

faqs.q: What is the deed transfer tax in Buncombe County?
faqs.a: North Carolina charges $1.00 on each $500 of the price or fraction of it. The seller pays it to the register of deeds before the deed is recorded, and half stays with the county.

faqs.q: What happens if my deed is not on standard paper in Buncombe County?
faqs.a: The office can still record it, but charges a $25 non-standard fee on top of the regular recording fee. Standard means 8.5 by 11 or 8.5 by 14 inch paper, black ink, 9 point type or larger, and the required margins.
